title: Restriction along an isomorphism is an equivalence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category that is closed, with equalizers and
coequalizers, such that $X\otimes-$ and $-\otimes X$ preserve colimits for every $X$. Let
$\varphi\colon\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be an isomorphism of monoid objects, with
$\mathcal R$ commutative. Then the restriction of scalars
$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\colon\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$
([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]) is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse
$\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}$.

proof.text:
Write $\psi=\varphi^{-1}\colon\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$. The morphism-of-monoids equations in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid] give
$\psi\circ\eta_{\mathcal S}=\psi\circ\varphi\circ\eta_{\mathcal R}=\eta_{\mathcal R}$ and
$\psi\circ\mu_{\mathcal S}=\psi\circ\mu_{\mathcal S}\circ((\varphi\circ\psi)\otimes(\varphi\circ\psi))=\psi\circ\varphi\circ\mu_{\mathcal R}\circ(\psi\otimes\psi)=\mu_{\mathcal R}\circ(\psi\otimes\psi)$.
Thus $\psi$ is a morphism of monoid objects. Apply [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] to $\varphi$ and $\psi$ to obtain
$F=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}\colon\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$ and
$G=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}\colon\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: First sentence: the inverse is again a morphism of monoid objects; expand the unit and multiplication equations.

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal S$-module object $(N,\gamma_N)$, applying the action formula of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] twice gives the action on $G(F(N))$:
$$\gamma_N\circ(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\circ(\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)=\gamma_N\circ((\varphi\circ\psi)\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)=\gamma_N.$$
The first equality is functoriality of tensoring with $N$, and the second uses $\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal S}$. The underlying object is $N$ and the underlying map of $G(F(h))$ is $h$ for every $\mathcal S$-linear $h$, by the same cited definition.

source.place: Composite restriction action formula and the displayed composite Res_{varphi^{-1}} after Res_varphi.

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal R$-module object $(M,\gamma_M)$, the same action formula of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] gives the action on $F(G(M))$:
$$\gamma_M\circ(\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\circ(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\gamma_M\circ((\psi\circ\varphi)\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\gamma_M.$$
Here functoriality of tensoring with $M$ and $\psi\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal R}$ give the equalities. The underlying object is $M$ and the underlying map of $F(G(k))$ is $k$ for every $\mathcal R$-linear $k$.

source.place: Last clause of the composite computation: similarly in the other order; write out the R-module action.

proof.text: Use the underlying identity maps to define $\eta_N\colon N\to G(F(N))$ and $\varepsilon_M\colon F(G(M))\to M$, together with their inverses. Steps 2 and 3 identify the respective actions, so the linearity condition in [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition] for each of these four maps reduces to $\gamma=\gamma$; their composites are identity maps. They form natural isomorphisms $\eta\colon\mathrm{id}_{\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)}\xrightarrow{\sim}G\circ F$ and $\varepsilon\colon F\circ G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)}$: by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], naturality on $h\colon N\to N'$ reads $G(F(h))\circ\eta_N=h=\eta_{N'}\circ h$, and on $k\colon M\to M'$ reads $k\circ\varepsilon_M=k=\varepsilon_{M'}\circ F(G(k))$. These are the data in the definition of a categorical equivalence with quasi-inverse $G$. If an adjoint equivalence is required, both triangle identities hold as well: $\varepsilon_{F(N)}\circ F(\eta_N)$ and $G(\varepsilon_M)\circ\eta_{G(M)}$ are underlying identity maps, hence identity module morphisms by the cited module-morphism definition.
